prompt: How does the ReAct agent work in our system?
chosen: The ReAct agent in the Agentic AI System implements a Thought-Action-Observation loop defined in the ReActAgent class in agentic_server.py. The process works as follows: 1) The agent receives a task via POST /v1/agent/run. 2) It constructs a system prompt listing available tools. 3) In each iteration, it calls Ollama for inference, producing a THOUGHT (reasoning). 4) It parses any ACTION: tool_name({params}) from the response. 5) The ToolExecutor runs the tool and returns the result as an OBSERVATION. 6) The loop continues until FINAL ANSWER is produced or MAX_ITERATIONS (default 10) is reached. The response includes all steps, tool calls, and the final answer.
rejected: The ReAct agent is an AI that can think and act. It uses tools and tries to answer questions. It goes through several steps to find the answer.

prompt: What is the VAT rate in Saudi Arabia?
chosen: The standard VAT rate in Saudi Arabia is 15%, increased from 5% to 15% in July 2020. There are three VAT categories: 1) Standard rated (15%): Most goods and services. 2) Zero-rated (0%): Exports of goods and services, international transportation, supplies of certain precious metals for investment. 3) Exempt: Certain financial services, residential real estate rentals, local passenger transport, and life insurance premiums. Businesses exceeding SAR 375,000 in annual revenue must register for VAT.

prompt: How do I deploy the system?
chosen: Deploy the Agentic AI System using Docker Compose with these steps: 1) Ensure Docker, Docker Compose, and NVIDIA Container Toolkit (for GPU) are installed. 2) Clone the repository and navigate to the project root. 3) Run 'docker-compose up -d' to start all four services: Ollama (port 11434), FastAPI API (port 8000), n8n (port 5678), and Redis (port 6379). 4) The model-loader container automatically pulls llama3.2:3b on first startup. 5) Verify deployment with 'curl http://localhost:8000/health' - check that ollama status is 'healthy'. 6) Access n8n at http://localhost:5678 (default credentials: admin/agentic123). Minimum requirements: 8GB RAM, 20GB disk. Recommended: 16GB RAM + NVIDIA GPU with 4GB+ VRAM.
rejected: Just use Docker to deploy everything. Run docker-compose up and it should work. Make sure you have Docker installed first.

prompt: What tools does the AI agent have access to?
chosen: The Agentic AI System provides seven built-in tools defined in agentic_server.py: 1) calculator - evaluates mathematical expressions using safe character filtering (digits, operators, parentheses). 2) web_search - searches the internet for current information (requires search API integration). 3) get_current_time - returns the current date/time in a specified timezone (default: Asia/Riyadh). 4) file_operations - reads, writes, and lists files restricted to ./data, ./output, ./temp directories with a 5000-char read limit. 5) http_request - makes GET/POST/PUT/DELETE requests to external APIs. 6) zatca_compliance - validates, generates, and checks status of ZATCA e-invoices. 7) send_webhook - sends JSON payloads to n8n webhook endpoints at http://localhost:5678/webhook/{name}.
rejected: The agent has tools like a calculator, web search, file reading, and some other ones. It can do math and search the web and stuff.

prompt: How do I add a custom tool to the system?
chosen: To add a custom tool to the Agentic AI System, follow these steps: 1) In agentic_server.py, add a ToolDefinition to the BUILTIN_TOOLS dictionary with name, description, and a JSON Schema parameters object specifying type, properties, and required fields. 2) Add a handler method to the ToolExecutor class (e.g., 'async def _my_tool(self, param1: str) -> str'). 3) Add an 'elif tool_name == "my_tool"' branch in the ToolExecutor.execute() method that calls your handler with the appropriate arguments. 4) Restart the FastAPI server. The agent automatically includes all BUILTIN_TOOLS in its system prompt, so it will be aware of the new tool. Make sure the tool description clearly explains when the agent should use it and what parameters it accepts.
rejected: You can add tools by modifying the code. Just add a new function and register it in the tools dictionary.

prompt: What is the difference between the /v1/chat/completions and /v1/agent/run endpoints?
chosen: These two endpoints serve different purposes: /v1/chat/completions (POST) is a direct LLM inference endpoint compatible with the OpenAI API format. It accepts a list of messages (system, user, assistant roles), forwards them to Ollama, and returns the model's response. No tool calling or reasoning loop is involved. Response time is fast (single LLM call). Use it for simple Q&A, translation, summarization. /v1/agent/run (POST) implements the full ReAct agent loop. It accepts a task description, optional context, and optional tool filter. The agent reasons step by step (THOUGHT), calls tools (ACTION), observes results (OBSERVATION), and iterates up to MAX_ITERATIONS times until producing a FINAL ANSWER. Use it for complex tasks requiring tool use, calculations, data retrieval, or multi-step reasoning. The response includes all steps, tool calls, and iteration count.
rejected: The chat endpoint is for chatting and the agent endpoint is for running tasks. The agent one is more powerful because it can use tools.

prompt: Explain how n8n workflows connect to the AI agent.
chosen: n8n integrates with the Agentic AI System bidirectionally: 1) n8n-to-Agent: n8n workflows trigger the agent via HTTP Request nodes. They can POST to /v1/agent/run with a task payload, or POST to /webhook/n8n with an event payload containing 'event': 'agent_task' and task details in 'data'. The webhook endpoint automatically creates an AgentTask and runs the ReAct loop. 2) Agent-to-n8n: The agent uses the send_webhook tool to push data to n8n. It sends POST requests to http://n8n:5678/webhook/{webhook_name} (Docker) or http://localhost:5678/webhook/{webhook_name} (local) with a JSON payload. n8n receives this via Webhook trigger nodes and can then execute downstream workflow steps like sending emails, updating databases, or calling external APIs. n8n is accessible at port 5678 with default credentials admin/agentic123.
rejected: n8n connects through webhooks. The agent can send data to n8n and n8n can call the agent. They talk over HTTP.

prompt: What is fine-tuning and when should I use it?
chosen: Fine-tuning is the process of further training a pre-trained LLM on domain-specific data to improve its performance on specialized tasks. For the Agentic AI System, you should consider fine-tuning when: 1) The base model (llama3.2:3b) doesn't have knowledge of your specific domain (e.g., ZATCA regulations, company-specific processes). 2) You need consistent output formatting (e.g., always responding in a specific structure). 3) You want to improve tool-calling accuracy for your specific tools. The recommended approach is QLoRA (Quantized LoRA), which loads the base model in 4-bit quantization and trains small adapter matrices on your data. This requires only a T4 GPU (16GB VRAM) and 15-20 high-quality instruction/output examples. After training, merge the adapter with the base model, convert to GGUF format, and import into Ollama using a Modelfile for local inference.
rejected: Fine-tuning means training a model on your own data to make it work better. You should do it when the base model doesn't know about your stuff.
